In the heart of a plague-ridden colony known as Darkhaven, amidst the decay of civilization, there lived a deaf-mute blacksmith named Thalion. His hands were as skilled with metal as the breath of life was with flesh, yet he was unable to hear the whispers of the world. Thalion’s companion, a scandal-tongued merchant named Seraphine, was known far and wide for her lips that could tell a tale quicker than a shadow passes at dusk.


Together, Thalion and Seraphine were chained to a stake in the central square, a silent testament to the colony's harsh punishments for those who dared to dream beyond the decrepit walls. Their chains were not merely of iron, but of despair, as their only hope of escape lay in an impossible task: to teach the colony's moths to carry their forbidden messages by feeding them drops of blood-soaked lies.


Thalion, with his deafness, communicated through the art of sign language, his hands dancing with desperate vigor. Seraphine, with her scandalous tongue, spun tales of freedom and beauty, her words painting pictures in the minds of any who would listen. Though they spoke different languages, their intentions were as one—a silent plea for escape.


The task was treacherous. The moths, creatures born from darkness, were not easily swayed. They hungered for blood, but they were not creatures of passion or reason. Thalion and Seraphine spent countless nights feeding the moths, each drop a lie about the outside world—a world they had never seen but dreamed of.
